summary: Reproduced the Inkling first-block tool-name leak in the prepared checkout for one-shot and streamed parsing, then fixed it by buffering ambiguous out-of-block text until the following control token determines whether it is a tool header. Added regression coverage for JSON and raw-text tool markers and boundary coverage for ordinary unframed output and continue_final_message.

tests.what_was_measured: Full reasoning-parser then FunctionCallParser pipeline. Both one-shot and 7-character streaming produced visible='get_weather' plus a valid get_weather({}) call for the missing-opener case; opener-present and thinking-first controls had empty visible content. Raw output: reports/j-b01d481bcf71/raw/reproduction-before.txt.
The same full parser pipeline produced empty visible content and a valid get_weather({}) call for all three cases in both modes. Raw output: reports/j-b01d481bcf71/raw/reproduction-final.txt.

367 focused parser tests passed, including the failing-before issue regression for 1- and 7-character streaming, both Inkling tool marker variants, and independent unframed/continuation boundaries. Raw output: reports/j-b01d481bcf71/raw/test-focused-final.txt.
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, secret, and relevant registration checks passed for changed Python files. Raw output: reports/j-b01d481bcf71/raw/pre-commit-final.txt.

gpu_evidence: The defect and correction are deterministic CPU-only parser state-machine behavior; no model execution or GPU kernel is involved. The assigned GPU was therefore not used.
remaining_limitations: No end-to-end request was run against real Inkling model weights, so model generation behavior and the reported hosted-session incidence were not measured.
No HTTP serving-path run was claimed; the retained fixture exercises the same reasoning-parser to tool-parser order without model inference.
An existing upstream candidate PR, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34051, was inspected before implementation and remained open at investigation time.
